comparisons.peer_summary: AMD develops world-class software stacks, including tools, compilers, and drivers, and works with customers to define customized solutions using its IP and design leadership.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and AMD disclose the development of comprehensive software stacks as part of their innovation and product strategy. NVIDIA explicitly states that it has built full software stacks running on top of its GPUs and CUDA to bring AI to major industries, listing specific proprietary stacks like DRIVE, Clara, and Omniverse. AMD similarly describes developing 'world-class software stacks' that include development tools, compilers, and drivers for its CPUs, GPUs, and FPGAs, while also emphasizing customized solutions. While NVIDIA focuses on industry-specific AI operating systems and full-stack AI integration, AMD’s disclosure highlights the foundational tools and drivers alongside custom IP integration.

sentences.text: Over the past 5 years, we have built full software stacks that run on top of our GPUs and CUDA to bring AI to the world's largest industries, including NVIDIA DRIVE stack for autonomous driving, Clara for healthcare, and Omniverse for industrial digitalization; and introduced the NVIDIA AI Enterprise software - essentially an operating system for enterprise AI applications.
We develop world-class software stacks that are used to enable our high-performance products.
Our software stacks include development tools, compilers, and drivers for our CPUs, APUs, GPUs and FPGAs.

comparisons.peer_topic: Software strategy and open source contributions
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel aims to optimize AI frameworks and maintains the OpenVINO toolkit for deep learning inference. In 2024, Intel launched the Open Platform for Enterprise AI under the Linux Foundation and contributed oneAPI specifications to the UXL Foundation to enable open, multi-vendor programming across accelerators.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies highlight the strategic importance of software in unlocking the potential of their hardware platforms, particularly in the context of AI. NVIDIA describes its software offerings, such as NVIDIA AI Enterprise, as an 'operating system for enterprise AI applications.' Intel mirrors this strategic focus by stating that 'software unleashes the potential of our hardware platforms across all workloads, domains, and architectures' and details its efforts to optimize AI frameworks (like PyTorch and TensorFlow) and launch open-source initiatives like the OpenVINO toolkit and the Open Platform for Enterprise AI to support generative AI use cases.

sentences.text: Over the past 5 years, we have built full software stacks that run on top of our GPUs and CUDA to bring AI to the world's largest industries, including NVIDIA DRIVE stack for autonomous driving, Clara for healthcare, and Omniverse for industrial digitalization; and introduced the NVIDIA AI Enterprise software - essentially an operating system for enterprise AI applications.

Our OpenVINO™ toolkit is an open source toolkit that accelerates deep learning inference on our processors across various use cases, such as generative AI, computer vision, audio, and language with industry standard models.
In 2024 we launched the Open Platform for Enterprise AI under the Linux Foundation to accelerate deployment of generative AI use cases through industry standard modular microservice architecture.

comparisons.peer_topic: AI research focus and on-device capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: The company conducts broad research and development across AI, including generative AI, with the goal of advancing core capabilities to run on-device and scaling them across industries, leveraging over a decade of investments focused on power efficiency and personalization.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and Qualcomm frame their innovation history around significant, long-term investments in Research and Development (R&D) focused on AI capabilities. NVIDIA quantifies its commitment by stating it has invested over $45.3 billion in R&D since inception to yield essential inventions. Qualcomm similarly characterizes its approach as conducting 'broad, leading research and development across AI, including generative AI' with over a decade of investments, specifically aiming to advance core capabilities for on-device execution and scaling across industries.

sentences.text: We have invested over $45.3 billion in research and development since our inception, yielding inventions that are essential to modern computing.

We conduct broad, leading research and development across AI, including generative AI, from fundamental research to platform and applied research, with the goal of advancing AI core capabilities to run on-device, and scaling them across industries and use cases.
With investments made in AI for over a decade, our research is diverse, and we are focused on power efficiency and personalization to make AI seamless across our everyday experiences.
